feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: New immigration court tactic leads to huge lines and chaos in Miami
entry.summary: Chaos unfolds at the Miami immigration court after judges are assigned mega master calendars, hearings where judges see more than 100 immigrants at once.

entry.title: Understanding the tech giants' oversized influence in American schools
entry.summary: Big tech companies like Apple and Microsoft use devices, training and conferences for teachers and students to embed in schools. The New York Times' Natasha Singer discusses the impact in Coding Kids.

entry.title: New lawsuits claim OpenAI execs put image ahead of safety in Canadian mass shooting
entry.summary: The suits say that recommendations to alert police about the alleged shooter were nixed by OpenAI's global affairs team, led by veteran political strategist Chris Lehane. OpenAI denies the claims.

entry.title: ICE detainee dies just hours after he was admitted into detention
entry.summary: Lianyong Wei's death marks the 57th death of an immigrant detainee held in the care of the government since the start of President Trump's second term. Twenty-four of those have occurred since Jan. 1.

entry.title: How will tariffs affect the midterms? In this Michigan border town, it's complicated
entry.summary: The recent trade war between the U.S. and Canada has both economic and political implications for Michigan, given it's the state's top trade partner.

entry.title: Whistleblower claims USPS plan for Trump's mail voting order could disrupt midterms
entry.summary: An anonymous federal official warned in a whistleblower complaint that a technical system the Postal Service built for mail voting is flawed and, if implemented, likely to disrupt the fall midterms.

entry.title: Whistleblower's lawyer warns USPS plan for Trump's order could keep ballots from voters
entry.summary: A lawyer for an anonymous whistleblower says Postal Service plans for an unusual verification rule, combined with a hastily built online system, could delay mail ballots from reaching eligible voters.

entry.title: Advocates say cities' aggressive clearing of encampments has caused more problems
entry.summary: A Supreme Court ruling two years ago allowed bans on sleeping outside. Homeless people and advocates in the Midwest say aggressive encampment clearing has caused problems.

entry.title: How Dolly Parton's literacy work affected Indigenous communities in Australia
entry.summary: In Australia, the queen of country music, Dolly Parton, is being remembered for her work in advancing children's literacy, particularly in Indigenous communities.

entry.title: The Clancy jury continues to deliberate
entry.summary: The jury in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the mother charged with murdering her three children, said it's not yet come to an unanimous decision. The judge has urged them to keep trying.
